title: Admin password card: never fails silently

steps.path: When YouCoded turns down a password request (it couldn't confirm your computer's admin program asked)
steps.headline: When YouCoded turns down a password request, the command's card says so in a yellow box instead of failing silently.
steps.changed: New. Before, the command just failed with 'no password was provided'. Now the card says: "YouCoded couldn't confirm this password request came from your computer's admin program, so it didn't ask for your password."
steps.notice: You always know why an admin command didn't ask for your password. The assistant is told too, so it can explain instead of retrying.
steps.risk: Rare in practice: it only appears on computers whose admin program the app can't verify.

highlight.text: YouCoded couldn't confirm this password request came from your computer's admin program, so it didn't ask for your password.

steps.path: What the assistant is told about sudo, per computer
steps.headline: The assistant is told exactly one true thing about sudo, depending on the computer it's running on.
steps.changed: Linux with a supported admin program: "sudo works: the user types their admin password in a card inside the app itself." Mac, or Linux the app can't support: "sudo only works here when the command needs no password." Windows: "sudo, if enabled on this PC, opens Windows' own permission window; it never asks for a password here."
steps.notice: The assistant never promises a password card that can't appear. The sentence is fixed for the whole time the app runs, so it doesn't cost extra, and a conversation moved to another computer gets that computer's sentence.
